newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria opens border with Iraq in rapprochement sign.
newsitem.headline: Syria opens border with Iraq in rapprochement sign.

text.p: Syria has opened its border with Iraq, closed since the beginning of the 1980s, to ease trade in a further sign of rapprochement between the two Arab states, a senior Syrian official said on Monday.

He told Reuters an Iraqi economic team would visit Syria on June 6 to discuss with Syrian authorities ways of importing Syrian goods in line with Iraq's oil-for-food agreement with the United Nations.
The reopening of Iraq's oil pipeline through Syria to the Mediterranean, closed for the past 15 years, was also under discussion, officials said.
"Two border points with Iraq in northeast Syria have already been opened and these will be used as a first stage by traders and businessmen of both countries," the senior official said.
But no decision had yet been made on the resumption of diplomatic ties which were severed in the early 1980s after Syria sided with Iran in its 1980-1988 war with Iraq.
The decision to open the border and the visit by the Iraqi economic follow a trip by a high-ranking Syrian economic delegation to Baghdad last month which was the first of its kind for over 16 years.
"I think the visits and the opening of the border, although they have an economic aspect, constitute a sign of more readiness by both countries to get closer to each other," one diplomat said.

Syrian officials said the re-opening of an oil pipeline which used to carry Iraq crude oil through Syria to the Mediterranean was under discussion but no decision had yet been made. The pipeline line was closed in 1982.

Oil industry sources said the longest part of the pipeline was being used at present to carry Syrian light crude from oilfields close to the Iraqi border and that rehabilitation of the line would be technically easy.

Syrian officials said the Iraqi economic team was expected to discuss during its Damascus visit the use of Syria's Mediterranean ports as transit points for Iraqi imports listed under the deal with the U.N.

Iraq's oil-for-food pact with the U.N. allows Iraq exports of $2 billion in six months to enable it buy food, medicine and other essential commodities for Iraqis hit by the sanctions imposed after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The deal, which started in December last year, comes under review on June 9.
